title: The Bosphorus Brief — Saturday, 12 September 2026
overview: A regionally quiet but legally consequential Saturday: courts and rights cases touching foreign residents dominate the substantive news, while the Central Bank held rates steady for a fifth straight meeting. Elsewhere in the wider region, tensions around Lebanon, Yemen's Red Sea corridor, and an Iraq-launched drone strike on a Saudi pipeline are worth watching for travel and shipping knock-on effects, though none currently touch Türkiye directly.
sections: <parameter name="heading">Legal security: Kavala retrial request, and a 25-year prison case
body: Osman Kavala has requested a retrial following a ruling from the European Court of Human Rights, a case closely watched by residents concerned with rule-of-law consistency in Türkiye (Independent Türkçe, DW). Separately, bianet reports that journalist and writer Erdal Süsem remains imprisoned after 25 years despite European court rulings in his favor — a stark reminder that ECtHR decisions do not always translate quickly into domestic outcomes. Neither case has immediate procedural implications for foreign residents, but both are useful barometers of how domestic courts respond to European rulings.
